$comment: Server-only question bank. Days cycle from #1 (2026-11-20). Answers, explainers and sources are only sent after a player locks a guess. min/max frame the reveal chart's log axis; answers must be typeable (under 1,000 trillion).

questions.q: How tall is Mount Everest, in metres?
questions.explain: China and Nepal announced the joint survey figure — 8,848.86 m — in 2020.

questions.q: How many people visited the Louvre in 2024?
questions.explain: Still the world's most-visited museum, though down from its 2018 record of 10.2 million.

questions.q: How far is the Moon from Earth on average, in kilometres?
questions.explain: You could line up about 30 Earths in the gap.

questions.q: How many seconds are there in a year?
questions.explain: 365 × 24 × 60 × 60. A leap year adds another 86,400.

questions.q: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.explain: Newborns have around 270; many of them fuse together as we grow.

questions.q: How tall is the Burj Khalifa, in metres?
questions.explain: The world's tallest building since 2010 — more than twice the height of the Empire State Building's roof.

questions.q: How fast does sound travel through air at 20 °C, in metres per second?
questions.explain: About 1,235 km/h — roughly a kilometre every three seconds.

questions.q: How many people were aboard the Titanic on its maiden voyage?
questions.explain: More than 1,500 of them died when it sank in April 1912.

questions.q: How much does a typical fair-weather cumulus cloud weigh, in tonnes?
questions.explain: The USGS estimate for a cloud of one cubic kilometre: about 1.1 million pounds of water, spread so thin it floats.

questions.q: Counting one number per second, non-stop, how many days would it take to reach one million?
questions.explain: 1,000,000 seconds is 11 days, 13 hours and 47 minutes. Counting to a billion would take almost 32 years.

questions.q: How many Earths could fit inside the Sun, by volume?
questions.explain: The Sun is about 109 times Earth's diameter — and volume grows with the cube.

questions.q: What is the average depth of the world's oceans, in metres?
questions.explain: The deepest point, Challenger Deep, is nearly three times that — about 10,900 m.

questions.q: About how many neurons are in the human brain?
questions.explain: The figure comes from a 2009 study that dissolved brains into a countable soup of cell nuclei.

questions.q: How long is the Great Wall of China, counting all its sections, in kilometres?
questions.explain: China's 2012 national survey measured every branch and section, built over two millennia.

questions.q: How many vertebrae are in a giraffe's neck?
questions.explain: The same as yours — a giraffe's are just much longer, up to about 25 cm each.

questions.q: How long does light from the Sun take to reach Earth, in seconds?
questions.explain: About 8 minutes 19 seconds. The light reaching you now left the Sun before you started this question.

questions.q: How much did Leonardo's ‘Salvator Mundi’ sell for at auction in 2017, in US dollars?
questions.explain: The most ever paid for a painting at auction, at Christie's in New York.

questions.q: What is the area of Australia, in square kilometres?
questions.explain: Nearly the size of the contiguous United States, with fewer people than Texas.

questions.q: If you could fold a 0.1 mm sheet of paper in half 42 times, how thick would it be, in kilometres?
questions.explain: Every fold doubles it: 0.1 mm × 2⁴² — thick enough to reach past the Moon.

questions.q: If you stretched out all the DNA in one human cell, how long would it be, in metres?
questions.explain: It's packed into a nucleus about six thousandths of a millimetre across.

questions.q: How fast does the International Space Station travel, in km/h?
questions.explain: Fast enough to circle Earth about every 90 minutes — around 16 sunrises a day for the crew.

questions.q: How tall is Hyperion, the tallest known living tree, in metres?
questions.explain: A coast redwood in California whose exact location is kept quiet to protect it.

questions.q: About how many stone blocks make up the Great Pyramid of Giza?
questions.explain: Built around 2560 BC, it was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for over 3,800 years.

questions.q: How many different games of tic-tac-toe are possible?
questions.explain: Counting every move order until someone wins or the board fills. Played perfectly, every game is a draw.

questions.q: How many countries are there in Africa?
questions.explain: 54 UN member states — more than any other continent.

questions.q: What is the hottest air temperature ever officially recorded on Earth, in °C?
questions.explain: Measured at Furnace Creek in Death Valley, California, on 10 July 1913 — still the World Meteorological Organization's official record.

source.name: Wikipedia: Highest temperature recorded on Earth

questions.q: About how many humans have ever been born?
questions.explain: The Population Reference Bureau's estimate. Around 7% of everyone ever born is alive today.

questions.q: How deep is the Kola Superdeep Borehole — the deepest hole humans have drilled — in metres?
questions.explain: Drilled in Russia from 1970. The rock at the bottom was about 180 °C.

questions.q: How many windows does the Empire State Building have?
questions.explain: It went up remarkably fast: construction started in March 1930 and it opened in May 1931.

questions.q: How long is one day on Venus — one full rotation — in Earth days?
questions.explain: Longer than its year: Venus orbits the Sun in just 225 Earth days.

questions.q: How long is the Trans-Siberian Railway, Moscow to Vladivostok, in kilometres?
questions.explain: The longest railway line in the world; the full trip takes about a week.

questions.q: How many possible combinations are there in a pick-6-from-49 lottery?
questions.explain: Buy one ticket a week and you'd expect to hit the jackpot about once every 270,000 years.

questions.q: What is the fastest wind gust ever recorded, outside of a tornado, in km/h?
questions.explain: Measured on Barrow Island, Australia, during Cyclone Olivia in 1996.

questions.q: How many flowers do honeybees visit to make one pound (about 450 g) of honey?
questions.explain: The National Honey Board's estimate. A single bee makes about a twelfth of a teaspoon in its lifetime.

questions.q: How tall is the Statue of Liberty, from the ground to the tip of the torch, in metres?
questions.explain: The copper statue itself is 46 m; the rest is pedestal and foundation.

questions.q: How far away is Proxima Centauri, the nearest star after the Sun, in kilometres?
questions.explain: 4.24 light-years. At Voyager 1's 61,000 km/h, the trip would take over 70,000 years.

questions.q: How long is the Panama Canal, in kilometres?
questions.explain: Ships climb 26 m through locks to cross Gatun Lake, then descend to the other ocean.

questions.q: Walking non-stop at 5 km/h, how many days would it take to walk around the equator?
questions.explain: The equator is 40,075 km around: 8,015 hours of walking.

questions.q: How tall is Angel Falls in Venezuela, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, in metres?
questions.explain: Its longest single drop is 807 m — the water often turns to mist before it reaches the bottom.

questions.q: How tall is the Mona Lisa, in centimetres?
questions.explain: The poplar panel is just 77 × 53 cm. Many visitors are surprised how small it is.
